a: The disjointed letters at the beginnings of surahs are generally among the ambiguous matters whose true meaning only Allah knows; in them is an indication of the inimitability of the Qur’an: it is composed of the very letters of which the Arabs’ language consists. The Arabs’ inability to produce its like — though they were the most eloquent of people — shows that the Qur’an is revelation from Allah. Opinions on interpreting these letters are many and varied.
